The legal precedents mentioned in the text are Smith v. Maryland and Jones v. United States. Smith v. Maryland established the third-party doctrine, which posits that individuals do not have a reasonable expectation of privacy for information voluntarily shared with third parties. Jones v. United States is cited as a case where this doctrine was applied, with the court referencing Smith to uphold the principle that voluntary disclosure to third parties negates privacy expectations.

The largest country in the world is Russia.
